affordance_in_statement: select exactly k of these allowed combinations ... every operator from 1 to k appears at least once
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task: because exactly k triples must cover k operators, each operator necessarily occurs exactly once. Only re-presenting the same requirement as an equivalent global exact-cover or 3-dimensional matching condition can avoid advertising the per-operator DFS decomposition, but it does not remove the underlying affordance.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Processes operators one at a time and chooses one triple for each, tracking apparatus and shift masks.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: select exactly k ... every operator from 1 to k appears at least once

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The attempted exact-cover search was too expensive and timed out on the worst-case input.
It enumerates candidate subsets with combinations, causing exponential-time behavior and TLE.
Its bitmask construction uses one bit per input triple, so with t up to k^3 it creates impractically large integer masks and crashes at runtime.

recommended_edit: No safe statement edit can defeat the surviving approach without changing the mathematical task: the exact-k and full-coverage conditions intrinsically imply one occurrence of every operator. If a presentational edit is required, describe the requirement directly as a 3-dimensional perfect matching/exact-cover condition rather than foregrounding the per-category coverage argument.
